paper_title: Knowledge Crosswords Geometric Knowledge Reasoning with Large Language   Models
caption: Problem distribution based on the correctness under the w/ knowledge and w/o knowledge settings using CoT and . The results indicate that while easier problems are mainly hindered by a lack of knowledge, the bottleneck for hard problems lies in geometric knowledge reasoning abilities.
model_annotation: The chart represents the distribution of problems based on correctness under different settings, categorized by difficulty level as easy, medium, and hard. There are three pie charts, each divided into four slices. The labels for the slices are N+K+, N-K+, N-K-, and N+K-, corresponding to distinct colors shown in a legend on the right side of the chart. For the "easy" category, the proportions are approximately 40.6% for N+K+ (green), 45.9% for N-K+ (yellow), 10.1% for N-K- (orange), and 3.3% for N+K- (red). The "medium" category shows similar proportions: 44.6% for N+K+, 44.3% for N-K+, 7.2% for N-K-, and 3.9% for N+K-. In the "hard" category, the proportions are more evenly distributed: 36.2% for N+K+, 36.8% for N-K+, 20.1% for N-K-, and 7.0% for N+K-. Each pie chart includes percentage labels inside the slices, and the chart includes a legend to identify the colors corresponding to each category. The slices are not visually emphasized or ordered in a particular way beyond their representation within each individual chart.
